chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
About the meat of horses, beasts of burden, mules, and donkeys, so he said: “It is halal (permissible), but people find it repugnant.”

key_terms.الدَّوَابِّ: beasts of burden or riding animals
key_terms.لُحُومِ: meats; the edible flesh being asked about
key_terms.يَعَافُونَهَا: they find it repugnant or dislike it

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of horses, mules, and donkeys halal in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the meat of horses, riding beasts, mules, and donkeys is halal (permissible). It also notes a social custom: although permissible, people generally dislike eating such meat.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4197 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as),

about the meat of horses, beasts of burden, mules, and donkeys.
Imam (as) said: "It is permissible, but people find it repugnant."
